 Adarsh, Madhav tons power UP to 100-run lead

 Anant Shekher Misra / TNN / Nov 04, 2026, 23:30 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Kanpur : Riding on centuries by debutant Adarsh Singh and Madhav Kaushik, hosts Uttar Pradesh secured a 100-run first-innings lead over Baroda after scoring 455 for eight at stumps on the penultimate day of their Ranji Trophy tie at Green Park on Wednesday. Adarsh slammed a record-breaking 162, the highest individual score by a UP debutant in the Ranji Trophy. He became the sixth UP batsman to score a century in his first match. The duo also registered a record opening partnership of 309 runs. For Baroda, off-spinner Mahesh Pithiya claimed five wickets, including the prized wicket of Adarsh Singh, all through leg-before-wicket dismissals. This was the eighth occasion in his career that he had taken five or more wickets in an innings. Resuming their innings at the overnight score of 196 without loss, Adarsh and Madhav added another 102 runs in the morning session, taking UP to 298 without loss at lunch. Adarsh completed his maiden first-class century in 157 balls, hitting 13 boundaries and a six. He reached the milestone by driving a delivery from Rasikh Dar through the covers for a boundary. Madhav followed him to the three-figure mark with a single off Mahesh Pithiya. He faced 195 balls and struck 12 boundaries to complete his century. Baroda finally broke the partnership after lunch when Madhav was caught behind by wicketkeeper MG Patel off B A Bhatt for 137. His innings included 15 boundaries and a six. Adarsh followed him back to the pavilion after being trapped leg-before by M Pithiya for 162, an innings studded with 17 boundaries and three sixes. UP were then 325 for two. Captain Aryan Juyal and Karan Sharma helped UP go past Baroda’s first-innings total of 355 and secure a crucial lead. However, the scoring rate slowed as the pitch became sluggish and the ball started keeping low. Bhatt provided another breakthrough by trapping Karan Sharma leg-before for 10. Pithiya then took charge, dismissing Rinku Singh (23), Siddharth Yadav (2), Prashant Veer (14) and finally skipper Aryan Juyal (67), reducing UP to 436 for seven. Juyal and Rinku had added 35 runs for the fourth wicket. Towards the end of the day, Atit Sheth dismissed Yash Dayal, who edged the delivery to wicketkeeper MG Patel. At stumps, UP were 455 for eight, with Shivam Mavi batting on 13 and Kartik Yadav yet to open his account. UP coach Gyanendra Pandey said the team would bat for another hour and try to add as many runs as possible to put pressure on the opposition. He added that the bowlers would need to maintain a good line and length, while the fielders would have to support them on the fourth day as UP would look to bowl out Baroda within 60 to 70 overs. Brief scores: Baroda first innings: 355 UP first innings: 455/8 (Adarsh Singh 162, Madhav Kaushik 137, Aryan Juyal 67, Rinku Singh 23, Prashant Veer 14, Shivam Mavi batting 13; Mahesh Pithiya 5/112, Bhargav Bhatt 2/138, Atit Sheth 1/61). BOX TON ON DEBUT Adarsh Singh – 162 KS Bhatia – 162 Almas Shaukat – 128 Mohindar Singh – 132 Priyam Garg – 117 SP Singh – 132
